defect: SessionService checked every two seconds but reacquired its 60-second non-reference-counted wake lock only after isHeld became false. Expiry could therefore release it before the next check; the device could sleep and cease to be READY.

platform_basis.conclusion: For a non-reference-counted WakeLock, acquire(timeout) removes the previous timeout callback and schedules a new one without first releasing the lock.

change: Renew the existing 60-second lease on each check only while the same authorization generation is valid, notifications are allowed, and ScreenPreparation reports READY. No new wakeup flag, no proactive waking of a sleeping or locked device, and no obsolete fifteen-minute session limit.
stop_and_timeout_boundary: Non-READY, stop, revoke and destruction keep their existing release paths. The last lease expires when Android runs its timeout callback; process death releases the Binder-owned lock. This is not an absolute wall-clock ANR or system-service guarantee.

host.method: Full production service with deterministic clock, non-reference-counted wake-lock timeout and Android lifecycle fakes
cases: PASS ready authorized session crosses original 60-second deadlines without release gaps
PASS lease renewal does not impose obsolete fifteen-minute session cap
PASS no more renewals means the last bounded lease expires
PASS screen-off and locked states release without waking or reacquiring
PASS authorization revoked before next tick releases and never renews
PASS stale generation cannot renew the new approval
PASS current notification stop releases immediately and cancels renewal
PASS disabled notifications stop control rather than silently retaining screen lock
PASS service destruction releases and removes pending renewal
PASS unsupported screen-lock level remains safe and does not create another lock
host.pre_fix_counterexample: The same suite with pre-fix production source fails the continuous 60-second-boundary assertion.

android_compile: passed for isolated debug test build; release build/signing is separate

emulator.platform: Isolated Android 16 / API 36.1 emulator, maintainer verification; not Muse or physical phone
emulator.conditions: Charging keep-awake disabled and screen timeout set to 15 seconds for both sides. Original settings saved and restored. No UI input or remote command during the measured intervals; passive power/activity sampling only.

before.result: Expired before renewal; entered Dozing/Asleep and did not reacquire automatically. This interval began near the end of an already-running lease, not at first acquisition.

after.scope: Crossed two original 60-second boundaries. Approximately 0.5-second sampling is supported by native power history, not a claim of universal timing.

owner_stop.maintenance_action: Normal Airtap notification Stop button, identified from screenshot and tapped locally

emulator.cleanup: Original power settings restored. Emulator left at Home, locally stopped, without silently restoring its synthetic grant. Server enrollment retained. No physical phone or production relay modified.
emulator.intervention: Notification discovery briefly used UIAutomator outside the quiet measurement interval and interrupted the service notification; the subsequent actual Stop check used a screenshot and normal tap. This is not counted as quiet-run stability.

physical_phone_causation: Not established. Code34 fixture CANCEL at 1532 ms and subsequent activity pause do not identify a wake-lock or power cause. Retain that failure and the successful later gesture independently.
code35_status_at_report: Fix included in separately signed code35, release build/lint passed and maintainer installation recorded. Muse code35 stability and original-pair results are not part of this emulator report.
privacy: Only result summaries and digests are published; raw power/activity dumps, local environment paths and session identifiers remain private.
